32:8: Then He made his offspring meaning his offspring from a lineage, he says: from the water that gushed forth and emerged from him. But he means from the shedding of its water, as the poet said: Then he came with a fierce, strong, and powerful sword, the offspring of a weak-willed man. His saying, from a despised water, means: from a weak, delicate sperm. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And He began the creation of man from clay, meaning the creation of Adam. Then He made his offspring, meaning his descendants, from a lineage of despised water, and the lineage is the despised, weak water. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Abu Yahya Al-A’raj, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, of a lineage, he said: clear water. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, From a weak water, he said: a weak sperm of a man, and degraded is a noun derived from the saying: So-and-so is degraded, which means he slipped and became weak.
32:9: God the Almighty says: Then He proportioned man, whom He began to create from clay, with a sound, balanced creation, and breathed into him of His spirit, so he became alive and speaking. “And He gave you hearing and sight and hearts. Little do you give thanks.” He says: And your Lord has bestowed upon you, O people, by giving you hearing by which you hear sounds, sight by which you see people, and hearts by which you understand good from bad, so that you may thank Him for what He has bestowed upon you of that. And His statement, Little do you give thanks, means: And you give little thanks to your Lord for what He has bestowed upon you.
32:10: God the Most High says: The polytheists who denied the resurrection said, Shall we then be lost in the earth? That is, our flesh and bones have become dust in the earth. There are two pronunciations for this: ḍalana and ḍalana, with the lam open or closed. The reading with the lam open is the most generous, and this is how we read it. It was reported from Al-Hasan that he used to read ʿaḍa ṣalana with the sad, meaning: we rot, from their saying: sala al-lahm and asl: if it rots. What these polytheists meant by their saying, Shall we then be lost in the earth? is if our bodies perish in the earth, because everything that is overcome by something else until it is hidden in what it overcomes, then it has been lost in it. The Arabs say: the water has been lost in the milk, if it has overcome it so that it cannot be distinguished in it. From this is the saying of Al-Akhtal to Jarir: I was the speck in a turbid, foaming wave, the one who brought it threw it as a gift of misguidance. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: If we are lost in the land, meaning: If we are destroyed. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, If we are lost on the earth, will we be destroyed? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, When we are lost in the earth, meaning: When we have become bones and crumbled remains, will we be raised up as a new creation? They disbelieve in resurrection. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And they said, ‘When we are lost in the earth, will we then be created again?’ He said: They said, When we are bones and dust, will we then be resurrected as a new creation? And His statement, Rather, they are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord, God Almighty says: These polytheists do not deny God’s ability to do whatever He wills, rather they are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord, out of fear of His punishment and fear of His retribution for their disobedience to Him. For this reason, they deny the meeting with their Lord in the afterlife.
32:11: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists: The Angel of Death will take your souls. He says: The Angel of Death, who is charged with taking your souls, will complete your number by taking your souls. From this, the rajaz poet says: Banu Adram are not from anyone, and the Quraysh do not equal them in number. Then to your Lord you will be returned. He says: After the Angel of Death takes your souls to your Lord on the Day of Resurrection, you will be returned alive as you were before your death, and He will reward the good among you for his good deeds, and the evildoer for his evil deeds. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: “Say: The Angel of Death who is set over you will take your souls.” He said: The Angel of Death will take your souls, and with him will be helpers from the angels. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, The Angel of Death will take you, he said: The earth was gathered for him and made for him like a basin from which he could take whenever he wished. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar.
32:12: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: If you could but see, O Muhammad, those who say, When we are lost in the earth, will we then be in a new creation? When they lower their heads before their Lord, out of shame before their Lord for their past sins in this world, they say, “Our Lord, we have seen what we used to deny of Your punishment of those who sinned against You, and we have heard from You the confirmation of what Your messengers used to command us to do in this world, so return us.” That is, return us to this world so that we may work in it in obedience to You, and that is righteous work. Indeed, we are certain. That is, we have now become certain of what we were ignorant of in this world, of Your Oneness, and that none but You should be worshipped, and there should be no Lord but You, and that You give life and cause death, and You resurrect those in the graves after death and annihilation, and You do what You will. And in a manner similar to what we said about his statement: They lowered their heads, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, his statement, And if you could but see when the criminals hang their heads before their Lord, he said: They were sad and ashamed.
32:13: God Almighty says: And if We had willed, O Muhammad, We could have given these polytheists from your people and others from the disbelievers guidance meaning: its right direction and success in believing in God. But the word from Me will come into effect meaning: the punishment from Me is obligatory for them. And His statement, I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together means with the people of sin and disbelief in God among them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And if We had willed, We could have given every soul its guidance. He said: If God had willed, He would have guided all people. If God had willed, He would have sent down to them a sign from the sky, and their necks would have remained humbled before it. But the word from Me will come into effect. The word will come into effect upon them.
32:14: God Almighty says: It will be said to these polytheists when they enter the Fire: Taste the punishment of God for forgetting the meeting with this Day of yours in this world. Indeed, We have forgotten you means: We have left you today in the Fire. And His statement: And taste the punishment of eternity means: It will also be said to them: Taste a punishment in which you will abide eternally for what you in this world used to do of sins against God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: “So taste for what you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours. Indeed, We have forgotten you.” He said: They forgot all good, but as for evil, they did not forget it. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Indeed, We have forgotten you, he said: We have left you.
32:15: God the Most High says: What confirms Our proofs and the verses of Our Book to the people who were reminded and admonished by them, “they fell down to God in prostration due to their existence, humbling themselves before Him, submitting to His greatness, and acknowledging their servitude to Him, and they glorify the praises of their Lord meaning: and they glorify God in their prostration with His praise, so they absolve Him of what the disbelievers describe Him as, and they attribute to Him of having a wife, children, partners, and equals, and they are not arrogant meaning: they do that, and they are not arrogant to prostrate to Him and glorify Him, and they are not disdainful of humbling themselves before Him and submitting to Him. It was said: This verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because some of the hypocrites used to leave the mosque when the prayer was called. This was mentioned by Hajjaj, from Ibn Jurayj.
32:16: God Almighty says: The south of those who believe in the verses of God, whose characteristics have been described, withdraws and rises from their beds in which they lie down for their desires, and they do not sleep calling on their Lord in fear and hope for His pardon for them, and His favor upon them with His mercy and forgiveness and from what We have provided them they spend in the way of God, and they perform from it the rights of God that He has made obligatory upon them in it. And it turns away: it interacts from the word al-jafa’, and al-jafa’ means prophecy, as the rajaz poet said: My friend, the one with the winds of Damascus, and Ibn Mallat, who is more gentle and affectionate Meaning: Her generosity is a characteristic of Ibn Mallat, and God Almighty described them as turning away from their beds because they left lying down to sleep, busy with prayer. The commentators differed regarding the prayer that God Almighty described them as having their sides turned away from their lying position. Some of them said: It is the prayer between sunset and night prayers. He said: This verse was revealed about people who used to pray at that time. Who said that? Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Abu Aruba, who said: Qatada said: Anas said, regarding His statement, They used to sleep but little of the night (al-Dhariyat 51:17), he said: They used to move between the sunset and evening prayers, and in this way their sides would turn away. He said: Ibn Abi Uday narrated to us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, regarding His statement, Their sides forsake their beds, he said: They pray between these two prayers. Ali bin Saeed Al-Kindi told me, he said: Hafs bin Ghiyath told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, Their sides forsake their beds, he said: between sunset and night prayers. Muhammad bin Khalaf told me: Zaid bin Hayyan told us: Al-Harith bin Wajih Al-Rasibi told us: Malik bin Dinar told us, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, that this verse was revealed about some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who used to pray between sunset and night prayers, their sides forsaking their beds. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Muhammad ibn Bishr told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Aruba, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas: Their sides forsake their beds. He said: They used to perform voluntary prayers between sunset and night prayers. He said: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Anas, Their sides forsake their beds. He said: Between sunset and night prayers. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, Their sides forsake their beds. He said: They used to perform voluntary prayers between the sunset prayer and the evening prayer. Others said: It means the Maghrib prayer. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said: My father told me, on the authority of Talha, on the authority of Ata’, Their sides forsake their beds. He said: On the night. It was reported on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Yahya bin Saifi said, on the authority of Abu Salamah, who said: The darkness. Others said: To wait for the Isha prayer. Who said that? Abdullah bin Abi Ziyad told me: Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah Al-Awisi told us, on the authority of Sulayman bin Bilal, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, that this verse, Their sides forsake their beds, was revealed regarding waiting for the prayer called the ‘Isha’ prayer. Others said: It means standing at night. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, Their sides forsake their beds, he said: standing at night. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Their sides forsake their beds, he said: These are those who stay up at night to pray. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, Their sides forsake their beds means they get up to pray at night. Others said: This is a description of a people whose tongues never fail to mention God. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement, Their sides forsake their beds to invoke their Lord in fear and hope, that they are a people who do not cease to remember God, whether in prayer, or standing, or sitting, or when they wake up from their sleep. They are a people who do not cease to remember God. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding His statement, Their sides forsake their beds...to the end of the verse. He says: They forsake their beds for the remembrance of God. Every time they wake up, they remember God, either in prayer, or standing, or sitting, or lying on their sides. So they do not cease remembering God. The correct thing to say about this is that God described these people as having sides that turn away from their beds, being busy with supplication to their Lord and worshipping Him out of fear and food. This is because their sides turn away from their beds at night, because what is known about a describer describing a man as having his sides turned away from his bed is only a description of him as having avoided sleep at the time when people sleep, which is night and not day. This is how the Arabs describe a man when they describe him with this. This is indicated by the statement of Abdullah bin Rawahah al-Ansari, may God be pleased with him, in describing the Prophet of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: He spends the night turning away from his bed when the polytheists make his beds heavy. If this is the case, and God, the Exalted, did not specify in His description of these people the way He described them, that their sides forsake their beds, in terms of the conditions and times of the night, one condition or time rather than another, then it is obligatory for this to apply to all hours and times of the night. If this is the case, then whoever prays between Maghrib and Isha, waits for the last Isha, or stands in prayer at night or part of it, or remembers God during the hours of the night, or prays Isha, is among those included in the apparent meaning of His statement, Their sides forsake their beds, because his side has been forsaken from his bed when he stood up to pray, prayed or remembered God, or sat after he was no longer lying down and he was able to stand or sit. However, even if this is the case, directing the speech to the fact that it refers to the night prayer is more pleasing to me, because that is the most obvious meaning, and most likely according to the apparent meaning of the speech, and it is the same as the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is what Ibn Al-Muthanna told us. He said: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us. He said: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam. He said: I heard Urwah bin Al-Zubayr narrating on the authority of Mu`adh bin Jabal that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Shall I not guide you to the doors of goodness? Fasting is a shield, charity expiates sin, and the servant standing in prayer in the depths of the night. And he recited this verse: Their sides forsake their beds to invoke their Lord in fear and hope, and they spend out of what We have provided them. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Yahya bin Hammad told us: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit and Al-Hakam, on the authority of Maymun bin Abi Shabib, on the authority of Muadh bin Jabal, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani told me: Adam told us: Sufyan told us: Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir told us, on the authority of al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, on the authority of Maimun ibn Abi Shabib, on the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: If you wish, I will inform you of the gates of goodness: fasting is a shield, charity expiates sin, and a man standing in the dead of night. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: Their sides forsake their beds. Abu Kurayb told us: Yazid bin Hayyan told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, who said: Asim bin Abi Al-Najud told us, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Muadh bin Jabal, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: Their sides forsake their beds, he said: The servant’s standing at night. Abu Hammam Al-Walid bin Shuja’ told us: My father told me: Ziyad bin Khaithama told me, on the authority of Abu Yahya, the qat seller, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned the night prayer, and his eyes overflowed with tears until his tears flowed. Then he said: Their sides forsake their beds. As for his saying, They call upon their Lord in fear and hope... the verse, the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about it. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: They call upon their Lord in fear and hope, and from what We have provided them, they spend. He said: Out of fear of God’s punishment, and hope for God’s mercy, and from what We have provided them, they spend in obedience to God and in His path.
32:17: God Almighty says: No soul knows what God has hidden for those whom He, the Most High, described in these two verses, what their eyes will be comforted by in His Paradise on the Day of Resurrection. As a reward for what they used to do. He says: As a reward for the deeds they used to do in this world. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told me: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, who said: Abdullah said: It is written in the Torah: God has prepared for those who forsake their beds what no eye has seen, what has not entered into the heart of man, what no ear has heard, and what no angel brought near has heard. He said: And we recite it: No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes. Khallad told us, he said: Al-Nadr bin Shumayl told us, he said: Israel told us, he said: Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of Ubaidah bin Rabi’ah, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, he said: It is written in the Torah about God for those who forsake their beds what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, in the Qur’an: No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes as reward for what they used to do. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: There is hidden for them that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never crossed the mind of man. Sufyan said: As far as I know, without a doubt. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Abu Ubaydah, who said: `Abdullah said: He meant God: I have prepared for My righteous servants that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no heart has conceived. No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes as reward for what they used to do. Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Salt told us, on the authority of Qais ibn al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Ubaydah ibn Rabi’ah al-Harithi, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, who said: Indeed in the Torah: For those who forsake their beds there is an honor which no eye has seen, no human heart has conceived, and no ear has heard. And indeed in the Qur’an: No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Al-Ashja’i narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abjar, who said: I heard Al-Sha’bi say: I heard Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah say on the pulpit: “Moses, peace be upon him, was asked about the person with the lowest share in Paradise. He was told: A man will be brought when the people of Paradise have entered Paradise. He will be told: Enter. He will say: Where are you, when the people have neglected their rights? He will be told: Count four kings from the kings of this world. You will have the same as they had, and another will be given to you for your own pleasure. He will say: I desire such and such, and I desire such and such. It will be told: You will have another, for you the delight of your eyes. He will say: The delight of such and such. It will be told: You will have ten times the same. And he was asked about the person with the greatest share in Paradise. He said: That is something that was sealed on the day the heavens and the earth were created. Al-Sha’bi said: It is in the Qur’an: ‘No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes as reward for what they used to do.’” Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi told me: al-Humaidi told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, and al-Qarqasani told me about it, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Mutraf ibn Tarif and Ibn Abjar, who heard al-Sha’bi say: I heard al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah on the pulpit, raising it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Moses asked his Lord: ‘O Lord, which of the people of Paradise has the lowest status?’ He said: ‘A man will come after the people of Paradise have entered Paradise.’ It will be said to him: ‘Enter.’ He will say: ‘How can I enter when they have settled in their stations?’ It will be said to him: ‘Would you be satisfied to have the same as what a king of the world had?’ He will say: ‘Blessed, O Lord, I am satisfied.’ It will be said to him: ‘You have this and the like of it and the like of it and the like of it.’ He will say: ‘I am satisfied, O Lord, I am satisfied.’ It will be said to him: ‘You have this and ten times as much with it.’ He will say: ‘I am satisfied, O Lord.’ It will be said to him: ‘In addition to this, you will have whatever your soul desires and your eyes delight in.’ Moses said: ‘O Lord, which of the people of Paradise has the highest status?’ He said: ‘I intended it, and I will tell you about them.’” I have planted my dignity for them with my own hand, and sealed it, so that no one has seen it, no ear has heard it, and no human heart has conceived it. He said: The proof of that is in the Book of God: No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes as reward for what they used to do. Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Tusi narrated to us: Ishaq ibn Sulayman narrated to us: Amr ibn Abi Qays narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Layla, on the authority of al-Minhal ibn Amr, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, And His Throne was over the water (Hud 11:7), “The Throne of God was over the water, then He took for Himself a garden, then He took another beneath it, then He covered it with a single pearl. He said: And beneath them are two gardens.” He said: They are the ones that no soul knows, or he said: They are the ones that no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes, as reward for what they used to do. He said: They are the ones that the creation does not know what is in them, or what is in them, every day there comes to them from it or from them a gift. Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, in a similar manner. Sahl ibn Musa al-Razi narrated to us: Al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, on the authority of Safwan ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu al-Yaman al-Hawzani or someone else, who said: “Paradise has one hundred levels, the first of which is silver, its floor is silver, its dwellings are silver, its vessels are silver, and its soil is musk. The second is gold, its floor is gold, its dwellings are gold, its vessels are gold, and its soil is musk. The third is pearls, its floor is pearls, its dwellings are pearls, its vessels are pearls, and its soil is musk. And ninety-seven after that are what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.” Then he recited this verse: No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes as reward for what they used to do. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Al-Maharibi and Abd al-Rahim narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God said: I have prepared for My righteous servants that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. And if you wish, you may recite: God said: ‘No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes as reward for what they used to do.’” Abu Kurayb narrated: Abu Mu’awiyah and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have prepared for My righteous servants that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never crossed the mind of man. Abu Hurayrah said: Who has this to tell you? Read, if you wish, No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes as reward for what they used to do. Abu Hurayrah said: We recite it: comfort for eyes. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Hakam ibn Abaan, on the authority of Al-Ghatrif, on the authority of Jabir ibn Zayd, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of the Trustworthy Spirit, who said: “The servant’s good deeds and his bad deeds will be brought forth, and they will be diminished by one another. If even one good deed remains, God will expand his space for him in Paradise.” He said: So I entered upon him and he increased it, and he narrated something similar to this. He said: “I said: ‘So where did the good deed go?’ He said: ‘Those are the ones from whom We will accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds. They will be among the companions of Paradise—the promise of truth which they were promised.’” (al-Ahqaf 46:16). I said: His statement, No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes, means: The servant does a secret that he confides in God and that the people do not know about, so God will confide in him on the Day of Resurrection a comfort for his eyes.” Al-Abbas ibn Abi Talib told me, he said: Ma’la ibn Asad told us, he said: Salam ibn Abi Mut’i’ told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Uqba ibn Abd al-Ghafir, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrating on the authority of his Lord, he said: I have prepared for My righteous servants that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Abu Sakhr told me, that Abu Hazim told him, he said: I heard Sahl bin Sa’d say: I witnessed a session with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in which he described Paradise until he finished. Then he said at the end of his hadith: In it is that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Then he recited this verse: Their sides forsake their beds... until His saying: A recompense for what they used to do. Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: It has reached me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Your Lord said: I have prepared for My servants who have believed and done righteous deeds that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.” Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrated this on the authority of his Lord: “Your Lord said: I have prepared for My righteous servants that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never crossed the mind of man.” Ibn Wakee’ told us: Sahl bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan: No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes. He said: They concealed a deed in this world, so God rewarded them for their deeds. Al-Qasim bin Bishr told me, he said: Sulayman bin Harb told us, he said: Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Abu Rafi’, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. Hammad said: I think it was on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Whoever enters Paradise will be blessed and will not be miserable. His clothes will not wear out, and his youth will not fade. In Paradise there is that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never crossed the mind of man.” The reciters differed in their reading of the verse, No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes. Some of the Medinans and Basrans, and some of the Kufians, read it as akhfa with a damma on the alif and a fatha on the ya’, meaning to do. Some of the Kufians read it as akhfa lahum with a damma on the alif and a fatha on the ya’, meaning to do, I akhfa lahum ana. The correct thing to say about this, according to us, is that they are two well-known readings, close in meaning, because if God conceals something, then it is concealed, and if He conceals, then He has no concealer other than Him. And ma in His statement, No soul knows what has been concealed for them, if it is made to mean that, then it is in the accusative case, with the occurrence of knows, as the reciter recited, then it is concealed. And if it is directed to the meaning of, i.e., it is in the nominative case, if it is recited, then it is concealed with the accusative of the ya’ and the damma of the alif, because its agent is not named. And if it is recited, then it is in the accusative case, with the occurrence of hidden, as it is.
32:18: God the Most High says: Is this disbeliever who denies the promise and threat of God, who disobeys the commands and prohibitions of God, like this believer in God, who believes in His promise and threat, who obeys Him in His commands and prohibitions? No! They are not equal before God. He says: The disbelievers in God and the believers in Him are not equal before Him in what He will do to them on the Day of Resurrection. He said they are not equal in the plural, but He only mentioned two before that: a believer and a sinner, because He did not mean by believer one believer, and by sinner one sinner, but rather He meant all sinners and all believers in God. So if the two are not equal, the Arabs used the plural method. It was mentioned that this verse was revealed about Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and Al-Walid ibn Uqba. Who said that? Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah ibn al-Fadl told us: Ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of some of his companions, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar, who said: This verse was revealed in Medina concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib and al-Walid ibn Uqba ibn Abi Mu’ayt. There was some talk between al-Walid and Ali, and al-Walid ibn Uqba said: I am more eloquent than you, sharper in my spear, and more capable of striking a battalion than you. Ali said: Be quiet, for you are a sinner. So God revealed concerning them both: Is he who is a believer like he who is a sinner? They are not equal.... to His saying: You deny him. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Is he who is a believer like he who is a sinner? They are not equal. He said: By God, they are not equal in this world, nor at death, nor in the Hereafter.
32:19: And His statement, As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them are the Gardens of Refuge, meaning the gardens of dwellings in which they will reside in the Hereafter and to which they will return. And His statement, as a reward for what they used to do, means: as a reward for what He has sent them down to as a reward from Him for what they used to do in this world in obedience to Him. And His statement, As for those who disbelieved, God Almighty says: As for those who disbelieved in God and abandoned His obedience, their refuge is the Fire, meaning: their dwellings to which they will return in the Hereafter are the Fire. Whenever they want to leave it, they will be returned to it and it will be said to them, 'Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny, in this world, that God had prepared it for the people of polytheism. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that?
32:20: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And as for those who were wicked, they associated others with God, and it will be said to them, ‘Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny.’ And the people are liars, as you can see.
32:21: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the lower punishment that God promised to make these wicked people taste. Some of them said: It is the calamities of this world in lives and wealth. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We will make them taste of the lesser punishment. He said: The calamities, illnesses, and trials of this world with which God tests His servants until they repent. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And We will surely make them taste of the lesser punishment before the greater punishment that perhaps they will return. He said: The lesser punishment is the affliction of this world. It was said: It refers to the calamities. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Arni, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka’b: And We will surely make them taste of the nearer punishment. He said: The calamities in this world. He said: And the smoke has already passed, and the strike and the binding. Abu Musa said: Yahya bin Saeed left Yahya bin Al-Jazzar, a man missing. Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Saeed and Muhammad ibn Ja`far narrated to us, saying: Shu`bah narrated to us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-`Arni, on the authority of Yahya ibn Al-Jazzar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Layla, on the authority of Abi ibn Ka`b, that he said: Concerning this verse, And We will surely make them taste of the lesser punishment before the greater punishment, he said: The calamities of this world, and the necessity and the strike, or the smoke. Shu`bah was unsure about the strike or the smoke. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Urwa, on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-`Arni, on the authority of Yahya Ibn Al-Jazzar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Abi Ibn Ka`b, in a similar manner, except that he said: calamities, adhering to them, and striking them. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Zaid bin Habbab told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Arni, on the authority of Yahya bin Al-Jazzar, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Laila, on the authority of Abi bin Ka’b, who said: The calamities that befall people in this world are: the blow, the smoke, and the sticking. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Abu Ja’far al-Razi, on the authority of al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu al-A’lya: And We will surely make them taste of the nearer punishment. He said: The calamities in this world. He said: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak: And We will surely make them taste of the lesser punishment before the greater punishment. He said: The calamities in their worldly life and their wealth. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he told him, on the authority of Al-Hasan, his statement, And We will make them taste of the lesser punishment: meaning the calamities of this world. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim: And We will surely make them taste of the lesser punishment. He said: Things that they will be afflicted with in this world. Others said: It means the borders. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Shabib, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And We will surely make them taste the lesser punishment before the greater punishment. He said: The prescribed punishments. Others said: It meant killing with the sword. He said: And they were killed on the day of Badr. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, And We will make them taste of the nearer punishment. He said: The day of Badr. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, similarly. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Israel told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, the same. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Aouf told us, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Ali, that he said: And We will surely make them taste of the lesser punishment before the greater punishment. He said: Killing with the sword patiently. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abd Al-A’la told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith bin Nawfal: And We will surely make them taste the lesser punishment before the greater punishment. He said: Killing by the sword. Everything that God has promised this nation of the lesser punishment is the sword. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And We will surely make them taste of the lesser punishment before the greater punishment. He said: Killing and hunger for the Quraysh in this world. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Mujahid used to narrate on the authority of Abi bin Kaab that he used to say, And We will surely make them taste of the lesser punishment before the greater punishment: on the day of Badr. Others said: He meant by that the years that befell them. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, And We will surely make them taste of the lesser punishment before the greater punishment. He said: Years befell them. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, the same. Others said: What he meant by that is: the torment of the grave. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said: Ubaid God told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid: And We will surely make them taste of the lesser punishment before the greater punishment. He said: The lesser punishment is in the graves and the punishment of this world. Others said: This is the torment of this world. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And We will surely make them taste of the lesser punishment, he said: The lesser punishment is the punishment of this world. The first statement on this matter is to say: God promised these immoral people who denied His threat in this world the lesser punishment, that We would make them taste it without the greater punishment. And the punishment is whatever calamity befell them in this world, whether severe famine or killing, or calamities that befall them. All of that is from the lesser punishment, and God Almighty did not specify its mention, since He promised them that He would punish them with one type of that without another type. And He punished them with all of that in this world with killing, hunger, hardships, and calamities in wealth, so He fulfilled what He promised them. His saying, Before the greater punishment, means: before the greater punishment, which is the punishment of the Day of Resurrection. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah: Below the greatest punishment, he said: On the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Israel told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, similarly. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, below the greatest punishment on the Day of Resurrection in the Hereafter. Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said: Ubaid God told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid, before the greatest punishment on the Day of Resurrection. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Below the greatest punishment on the Day of Resurrection. Qatada told it, on the authority of Al-Hasan. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, below the greater punishment, he said: The greater punishment is the punishment of the Hereafter. His saying, Perhaps they will return, means: so that they will return and repent by being punished with the lowest punishment. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah: Perhaps they will return. He said: They will repent. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Abu Ja’far al-Razi, on the authority of al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu al-Aliyah: Perhaps they will return, he said: They will repent. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Perhaps they will return: meaning, repent.
32:22: God Almighty says: Who among people is more unjust to himself than he who is admonished by God with His proofs, the verses of His Book, and His Messengers, but then turns away from all of that, so he does not take heed of His admonitions, but rather is arrogant towards them? His saying, Indeed, We will take retribution from the criminals, means: We will take retribution from those who have committed sins and evil deeds. Some of them said: What is meant by criminals in this context are: the people of destiny. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Marwan bin Muawiyah told us: Wa’il bin Dawud told us, on the authority of Marwan bin Sufayh, on the authority of Yazid bin Rafi’, who said: God’s statement in the Qur’an, Indeed, We will take retribution from the criminals, refers to the people of destiny. Then he recited, Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness (al-Qamar 54:47) until His statement, We created it with predestination (al-Qamar 54:49). Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us, he said: Marwan told us, he said: Wa’il bin Dawud told us, on the authority of Ibn Sufayh, on the authority of Yazid bin Rafi’, something similar, except that he said in his hadith: Then Wa’il bin Dawud recited these verses Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness (al-Qamar 54:47)... to the end of the verses. Others said about this, including: Imran bin Bakkar Al-Kila’i narrated to me, he said: Muhammad bin Al-Mubarak narrated to us, he said: Ismail bin Ayyash narrated to us, he said: Abdul Aziz Ubaid God narrated to us, on the authority of Ubadah bin Nassi, on the authority of Junada bin Abi Umayya, on the authority of Muadh bin Jabal, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Three things, whoever does them has committed a sin: whoever accepts a banner unjustly, or disobeys his parents, or walks with an oppressor, supporting him, has committed a sin. God says: ‘Indeed, We will take retribution from the criminals.’”
32:23: God Almighty says: And We gave Moses the Torah, just as We gave you the Criterion, O Muhammad. So be not in doubt about meeting Him. He says: So be not in doubt about meeting Him. Qatada used to say: The meaning of that is: So be not in doubt about meeting Him, or that you will meet Him on the Night Journey. And this is what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, reported. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah Al-Riyahi, he said: The cousin of your Prophet, meaning Ibn Abbas, told us, he said: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “On the night of my Night Journey, I saw Moses, son of Imran, a tall, curly-haired man, as if he were from the men of Shanu’ah. I saw Jesus, a man with a medium build, reddish-white complexion, with a smooth head. I saw Malik, the keeper of Hellfire, and the Antichrist, in the signs that God showed him, so do not be in doubt about meeting him, for he saw Moses and met Moses on the night of his Night Journey.” And His statement, And We made him a guidance for the Children of Israel, God Almighty says: And We made Moses a guidance for the Children of Israel, meaning: a guidance for them so that they would be guided by following him, and attain the truth by imitating him and adhering to his words. And what we said about that was said by the people of interpretation. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel, he said: God made Moses a guidance for the Prophet of Israel.
32:24: And His statement, And We made from among them leaders, God Almighty says: And We made from among the Children of Israel leaders, which is the plural of leader, and the leader is the one who is followed in good or evil, and what is meant by that in this place is that He made leaders in good, who are followed and whose guidance is followed. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And We made from among them leaders guiding by Our command, he said: leaders in goodness. And His statement, guiding by Our command, God Almighty says: they guide their followers and those who accept them by Our permission for them to do so, and by Our strengthening them for it. And his saying, When they were patient, the reciters differed in their recitation of that. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the people of Kufa, recited it as when they were patient with a fatha on the lam and a shaddah on the meem, meaning: when they were patient, and when they were patient. The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it as when with a kasra on the lam and a soft meem, meaning: because of their patience in refraining from the world and its desires, and their striving in obeying Us, and working according to Our command. It was mentioned that that is in the recitation of Ibn Mas’ud as by what they were patient. When the lam of when is broken, it is in the position of a genitive case. If the lam is opened and the meem is doubled, then it has no position because it is then a tool. In my opinion, they are two well-known readings with similar meanings. Both of them have been read by most reciters, so whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct. The interpretation of the statement, when read with a fat-ha on the lam and a shaddah on the meem, is: “And We made from among them leaders guiding their followers by Our permission to them and by strengthening them for guidance, as they were patient in obeying Us and turned away from the pleasures and desires of this world.” If it is read with a kasra on the lam, it is as we have described. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said: My father said: We heard in And We made from among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient he said: about the world. And His statement, And they were certain of Our signs, means: They were people of certainty in what Our proofs showed them, and people of belief in what was made clear to them of the truth, and faith in Our messengers, the verses of Our Book, and Our revelation.
32:25: God Almighty says: Your Lord, O Muhammad, will explain to all of His creation on the Day of Resurrection what they differed about in this world regarding matters of religion, resurrection, reward and punishment, and other matters of their religion. He will separate them with a decisive judgment by decreeing Paradise for the people of truth and Hell for the people of falsehood.
32:26: God Almighty says: Or did He not make it clear to them? As Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Did He not guide them? He said: Did He not make clear to them? And the reciters of the regions read this with the letter ya and this is the reading with us due to the consensus of the proof from the reciters, meaning: Did He not make clear our destruction of the past generations before them, our way with those who followed their path of disbelief in our verses, so that they would be admonished and warned. And his saying how many when guides is read with the letter ya is in the nominative case with guides. If it is read with the letter nun iw lam nahud, then the position of kam and what follows it is in the accusative case. And His statement, They walk in their dwellings, the Most High says: Or did He not make clear to them the great number of times We destroyed the past generations before them, walking in their lands and their lands, like Aad and Thamud? As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them - Aad and Thamud - and that they will not return to them. And His statement, Indeed in that are signs, means that God Almighty says: Indeed, in the empty spaces of the dwellings of the generations whom We destroyed before, these Quraysh who denied the signs of God, who were its inhabitants and builders by Our destruction when they denied Our messengers, denied Our signs, and worshipped other gods besides God, which they pass by and witness, there are signs for them and admonitions from which they may learn, if only they were people of reason and intellects. God says, Do they not hear God’s admonitions and His reminding them of His signs and making them aware of the locations of His proofs?
32:27: God Almighty says: Have these deniers not seen that by Our power We drive water to the dry, rough land in which there is no vegetation? Its origin is from their saying: a barren camel, if it eats everything, and likewise the barren land: that on whose back nothing remains except that it spoils it, similar to the barren camel eating everything it finds, and from it their saying for the gluttonous person: barren, as the rajaz poet said: Khab Jaruz, when he is hungry, cries and eats dates without throwing away the pits. Hence, the sword that leaves nothing behind when it cuts is called a Jaraz sword. It has four languages: Jaraz land, Jarz, Jarz, and Jarz, and the opening is for Banu Tamim, as far as I have heard. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The barren land is a land in Yemen. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A land in Yemen. He said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Abdullah bin al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Have they not seen that We drive the water to the barren land? He said: Clearer and similar. Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told me: Abd al-Razzaq bin Umar told us, on the authority of Ibn al-Mubarak, who said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar, except that he said: And the like of it from the land. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, to the barren land, he said: Barren land is that which does not receive rain except for rain that does not benefit it at all, except for what comes to it from floods. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Muhammad ibn Yazid told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: To the barren land means that there is no vegetation in it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa`id told us on the authority of Qatada: Have they not seen that We drive the water to the barren, dusty land? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, Have they not seen that We drive the water to the barren land? He said: The barren land is the one on which there is nothing, no vegetation in it. And regarding His statement, a barren plain (al-Kahf 18:8), he said: There is nothing on it and there is no vegetation in it or anything. Then We bring forth thereby crops from which their livestock eat and themselves God the Most High says: So We bring forth with that water that We drive to it despite its dryness and thickness and the length of its period of water, green crops from which their livestock eat and from which their bodies and beings are nourished and by which they live. Then do they not see? God the Most High says: Do they not see that with their eyes, so that they know from their seeing it that the power by which I did that is not impossible for Me to bring the dead back to life and raise them from their graves and restore them to the form they were in before their death.
32:28: God Almighty says, And they say, these polytheists, O Muhammad, when will this conquest come? There is disagreement about the meaning of this. Some of them said: It means: When will this judgment come between us and you, and when will this reward and punishment be? Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, And they say, ‘When will this conquest be, if you should be truthful?’ He said: “The companions of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘We have a day soon when we will rest and enjoy ourselves.’ The polytheists said: ‘When will this conquest be, if you should be truthful?’” Others said: Rather, he meant by that: the conquest of Mecca.
32:29: The correct statement regarding this is the statement of those who said: Its meaning is: And they say, When will this judgment come between us and you? They mean the punishment. This indicates that this is what is meant by His statement, Say, 'On the Day of Conquest, neither will their faith benefit those who disbelieve, nor will they be reprieved.' There is no doubt that God had granted the disbelievers the opportunity to repent before and after the Conquest of Mecca. If the meaning of His statement, When will this conquest was as stated by those who said, meaning the Conquest of Mecca, then there would have been no repentance for those of the polytheists who converted to Islam after the Conquest of Mecca. There is no doubt that God accepted the repentance of many of the polytheists after the Conquest of Mecca and benefited them through belief in Him and in His Messenger. Thus, it is known that what we have said about the interpretation is correct and that what contradicts it is invalid. His statement, If you are truthful, means: If you are truthful in what you say, then who will be punished for our denial of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and our worship of deities and idols? And His saying, Say on the Day of Conquest, means that He is saying to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to them on the Day of Judgment and the coming of the punishment: Those who disbelieve in God and His signs will not be prevented from believing in Him that they will at that time. As Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Say, ‘On the Day of Conquest, their faith will not benefit those who disbelieve.’ He said: On the Day of Conquest, when the punishment comes. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: The Day of the Conquest means the Day of Resurrection. The accusative case of the Day in His statement, Say, ‘The Day of the Conquest’ is in response to when, because when is in the accusative case. The meaning of the statement is: When will this conquest be, if you are truthful? Then it was said such and such a day, and this is how the reciters read it. And His saying, nor are they given respite, means: nor are they given a reprieve for repentance and review.
32:30: And His saying, So turn away from them and wait, for they are waiting, is saying to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So turn away, O Muhammad, from these polytheists who say to you: When will this conquest come, and who urge you to hasten the punishment, and wait for what God will do to them, for they are waiting for what you promise them of punishment and the coming of the Hour. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: So turn away from them and wait, for they are waiting, meaning the Day of Resurrection.
